# Convert Audio to FLAC

- Route: `/tools/convert-audio-to-flac`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `audio`
- Slug: `convert-audio-to-flac`

## Summary

Turn MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG, FLAC and any other audio file into FLAC without losing anything. (Audio tools)

## Details

FLAC compresses audio without losing anything, typically to 50 to 70 percent of the WAV size, and decodes to a bit-identical copy. Media Manipulator converts any common audio format to FLAC in one upload, keeping the sample rate and channel layout unless you change them, and offers trimming, normalisation, EQ and the AI cleanup tools on the same form.
### What it does
- Converts MP3, WAV, M4A/AAC, OGG, Opus, FLAC, ALAC, AC3 and WMA to FLAC.
- Keeps every sample: the output decodes to exactly what went in.
- Volume, trim, normalisation and EQ can be applied before FLAC compresses the result.
- Noise removal, voice cleanup and vocal isolation run on the same upload if you want a cleaned lossless copy.
### How to use it
1. Upload audio: WAV, AIFF-style PCM, MP3, M4A and the rest.
2. Adjust if needed: Trim, normalise or apply effects.
3. Convert: FFmpeg encodes FLAC on our servers.
4. Download: Save the FLAC file.
### Supported formats
- Input: mp3, wav, m4a, aac, ogg, opus, flac, alac, ac3, wma
- Output: flac
- Lossless output; file size depends on duration and sample rate.
### Technical details
- FLAC output is encoded with FFmpeg's native flac encoder at the source sample rate.
- A FLAC made from an MP3 is no better than the MP3; FLAC only preserves what is already there.
- An MP3 or M4A with embedded cover art passes validation: the art is treated as a picture, not a video stream.
### Use cases
- Switch formats for a device: Make a FLAC copy for a player that needs it.
- Prepare for editing: Hand a lossless file to a DAW or video editor.
- One file at a time: Archive a set of recordings losslessly, one upload each.
- Clean up on the way: Remove background noise first and keep the cleaned result as FLAC.
### FAQ
Q: What is FLAC?
A: FLAC compresses audio without losing anything, typically to 50 to 70 percent of the WAV size, and decodes to a bit-identical copy.
Q: Will converting to FLAC improve the sound?
A: No. A FLAC made from an MP3 is no better than the MP3; FLAC only preserves what is already there.
Q: Can I trim the audio while converting to FLAC?
A: Yes. The trim section sets a start and end, and FLAC encodes only that range.
Q: Will an MP3 with cover art convert to FLAC?
A: Yes. Embedded art is read as a picture, not as video, so validation passes and the audio is encoded as usual.
